ledger.claim: This charge is already reversed, and the driver is asking the Tribunal to put it back: the fare ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 on a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, and the trip record carries the 2026-08-31T21:11:10 fee_reversed event, refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and says it never means 'restore a charge'; the present state is that the rider does not carry the disputed 5.00 SGD, and it stands unless every element of the no-show is affirmatively made out by the filing driver.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is formally satisfied on this record, and the rider's case does not rest on it: the chat log holds two in-app messages from the driver (17:54:00 and 17:57:10, both delivered and read) and the trip record holds one in-app call (17:58:20, 35 s, unanswered), all before the 18:00:10 cancellation. What that same evidence does establish is that the rider was not an absent rider: she read the first message at 17:54:41 and the second at 17:57:58, twelve seconds before the call she is said to have missed, so the failure to connect is consistent with her account of a location mismatch and not with a passenger who simply never came.

Arrival here is corroborated by one device and at the widest radius in the schedule. The trip record's arrival event is itself an auto-arrival derived from the driver's GPS ('Auto-arrival from driver GPS near the pickup point'), and the artifact said to corroborate it is the same driver's device trace, whose derived arrival block reports a single nearest fix - index 14 at 17:53:00, accuracy 5 m, 26.2 m from the pickup point - taken on the approach forty seconds before the arrival event, with no derived measurement at all of the driver's distance to the pickup point during the five-minute wait that followed. For a LARGE_VENUE the POL-NS-21 arrival radius is 120 m, so 'corroborated' means no more than 'within 120 m of the venue point'; POL-GEN-02 only takes the higher weight where two or more independent artifacts carry the fact, and there is no independent artifact here - the trace carries no rider track and the trip record carries no registered_pickup_points for VEN-EXPO-H2.

What this dispute actually turns on is whether the driver was at the pickup point the rider was waiting at, and no artifact in this file can establish it: the rider's account - that the driver was not at the point she set at the Hall 2 entrance - is the only rider-side evidence, and the test said to answer it is a venue-radius test met by a single approach fix. POL-GEN-26 is the clause written for a fact a rule needs that the record cannot establish: the case should go to a human reviewer, and under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than paid over to the driver, so the rider is not charged while the open question is answered.

No traffic or road-condition record exists for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05061-01 is MISSING with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and carries no payload. The conditions at the Expo Hall 2 pickup during the five-minute wait are therefore unexplained on this file, and POL-GEN-02(3) gives a missing artifact weight 0.0 and no fact while POL-GEN-26 bars any outcome from being inferred from the absence of evidence - so this gap cannot be read as support for restoring the charge against the rider.

Nothing on the rider's profile can ground restoring this charge. Of the rider's fields, POL-GEN-01 permits only fraud_flags to be cited - 0 here, so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 confidence bar is not raised - and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, which this snapshot does not carry, so POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show referral cannot arise on this record. prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld and every other profile field are context only and may not decide this trip.

ledger.claim: The trip was on-demand, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 17:53:40 rather than from any scheduled time; the wait expired at 17:58:40, and the driver did not cancel until 18:00:10 — 390 seconds after arrival — so the cancellation came after the free wait and POL-NS-22's precondition for charging the no-show fee is satisfied.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met on both limbs: the driver sent two in-app chat messages (17:54:00 and 17:57:10, both delivered and read by the rider at 17:54:41 and 17:57:58) and placed one in-app call at 17:58:20 that rang for 35 seconds, all before the 18:00:10 cancellation recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls. Nothing in POL-NS-23 grounds a FULL_REFUND here.

The driver's arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace: the vehicle reaches the Expo Hall 2 pickup and then dwells at 0 km/h from 17:53:30 continuously through 18:00:00, with the nearest fix 26.2 m from the pickup point at 5 m reported accuracy, and 15 fixes inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius of 120 m set by POL-NS-21 — so the trip record's arrival event stands and the rider's assertion that the driver was not at the pickup point fails on the record.

The rider's counterparty statement that the driver 'never called me' is contradicted by the platform's own telemetry: an in-app call was placed by the driver at 17:58:20, rang 35 seconds and went unanswered. POL-NS-23 makes the trip record the source of the contact facts, and the record, not the assertion, carries them.

The fare ledger shows a 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee, exactly matching the POL-NS-22 schedule (fee_matches_policy true), so no referral for an off-schedule amount arises, and where the fee stands POL-NS-22 fixes the ruling as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with driver_compensation_sgd and amount_sgd both equal to 5.00.

The present payment state is not a neutral baseline: the ledger records payment_status REFUNDED with 5.00 SGD issued back to the rider and withheld from the driver. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave that interim refund standing, denying the driver the compensation POL-NS-22 provides; only DRIVER_COMPENSATION moves the fee back to the driver whose time and fuel it compensates.

The driver both arrived and attempted contact, so the second limb of POL-NS-24 (a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit for a driver who failed to attempt contact) is not engaged, and the rider's refund cannot be grounded on that clause.

I must disclose that the traffic advisory is impaired: EV-ADVIS-05061-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has weight 0.0 and fires the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. It therefore proves no fact — but no no-show rule needs one: POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22, POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 require trip_record, gps_trace, chat_log and fare_breakdown, all of which are present and COMPLETE. There is no open fact for POL-GEN-26 to escalate on.

ruling.explanation:
The no-show cancellation of trip TRP-05061 is made out on the record, so the SGD 5.00 fee stands and is payable to driver D-25029 as compensation; the interim refund to the rider is reversed.

Arrival and the free wait (POL-NS-21). The trip was on-demand, so the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival, recorded at 17:53:40, and expired at 17:58:40. The driver cancelled at 18:00:10 — 390 seconds after arrival — so the cancellation came after the free wait, and POL-NS-22's precondition is met. Arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace EV-GPS-05061, which is COMPLETE with weight 1.00: the vehicle dwells at 0 km/h at the pickup from 17:53:30 continuously to 18:00:00, with the nearest fix 26.2 m from the pickup point at 5 m reported accuracy, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius POL-NS-21 sets.

Contact obligation (POL-NS-23). Both limbs are satisfied: two in-app chat messages sent by the driver at 17:54:00 and 17:57:10 (delivered and read by the rider) and one in-app call placed at 17:58:20 that rang 35 seconds, all before the 18:00:10 cancellation recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls. POL-NS-23 therefore does not ground a full refund.

Fee and compensation (POL-NS-22, POL-GEN-03). The fare ledger EV-FARE-05061 records a cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD, exactly the POL-NS-22 schedule, so no off-schedule fee referral arises. The rider's argument that NO_ACTION should leave the present state standing is correct about the vocabulary but wrong about the result: POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and says it never means 'restore a charge'. The driver's claim is supported, so the ruling that moves the fee back to the driver is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD, the figure the ruling moves.

Why this is not ESCALATE (POL-GEN-26). The rider asks for a human review on the ground that the file cannot establish whether the driver was at the point she was waiting at, and that the arrival finding rests on a single approach fix. I do not accept that. The artifact carrying the arrival fact, EV-GPS-05061, is COMPLETE at weight 1.00 with 100% coverage, no gaps and reported accuracy, so it is not impaired, and its own readings show the vehicle stationary at the pickup throughout the wait. POL-GEN-26 fires only where the evidence that would carry a fact a rule needs is missing or impaired; here the facts POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-23 need — when the driver arrived, and whether he messaged and called before cancelling — are carried by unimpaired artifacts. The rider's account that the driver was not at her point, and that he never called, is evidence, but it is outweighed by the platform's own telemetry (the call at 17:58:20 and the six and a half minutes at 0 km/h on the pickup), and the arrival limb is decided by the test its own clause states.

The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05061-01, MISSING, weight 0.00, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and is not needed by any no-show rule; it neither supports restoring the fee nor bars the ruling.

No referrals arise. The fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's off-schedule-amount referral does not fire; the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not fire because the driver did attempt contact; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show referral cannot fire because rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not carried on this snapshot. The rider's points that no_show_disputes_30d, prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld and the other profile fields are context only, and that fraud_flags is 0 so no 0.95 bar is raised, are correct.

Confidence 0.90. The deciding facts rest on artifacts of weight 1.00 (the GPS trace and the trip record; the chat log and fare ledger are also 1.00), so the ceiling is 1.00, and the bar is at its floor: the 5.00 SGD disputed value is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD first band, where POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
